subject: design/read-to-rule-tech-design-v1
statement: The technical-design class gains **§0 "Read to rule"** as its first section, before §1, on the same terms `read-to-rule-v1` set for PRDs — four blocks (Judge these · Sanity-check the numbers · The author's open questions · Skip the rest), honest-zero forms, a one-screen cap, anchored routes — but **sourced from the design's own binding elements**: the ranked calls are the `**Decision:**` callouts paired with the `#ALT-n` they displaced, the numbers are the acceptance/DINV bounds, the open questions are §7, and the skip map names the design's downstream backstops. It ships as **template guidance plus one additive guide step** — the contract lives in tech-design-template's next version, and tech-design-new gains one step to author §0 last from the design's own content — and it **builds nothing** in docgate: `check-design-shape` and `lint-tech-designs` already ignore a leading §0 (they check header-closedness and mandatory-subsection presence, never an exact section set). §0 is **required for every design**, with an honest whole-section skip line for a design that genuinely routes nothing; the class has no PRD-style tiers, so there is no tier gate. The review-efficiency **capture line** `read-to-rule-v1` added at PRD gates is **deferred** for design gates (§3.4) — this decision delivers the routing section only.
